name: Mount Ingalls
summary: Mount Ingalls summit lookout (register: 1936) was taken down in 1984 and rebuilt at the Quincy fairgrounds; SummitPost says only the foundation remains on the summit.
design: 10-foot enclosed timber tower built to California Region 5 Plan BC-301 (register)
status_note: Dismantled in 1984 and rebuilt at the Plumas County Fairgrounds in Quincy; a hiking guide (SummitPost) says only the foundation is left on the summit
agency: US Forest Service, Plumas National Forest

access.note: The Quincy display is on the Plumas County Fairgrounds grounds; the sources read give no hours. The summit is in the Plumas National Forest, reached by logging roads from Lake Davis (SummitPost).

visit.trail_note: Round trip a little over 2 miles with about 525 feet of elevation gain, from a logging-road intersection (SummitPost).

events.note: Ed Merry working as lookout at the government station on the top of Mount Ingalls near Walker Mine; earliest station named in the sources read
Ed Merry resigned as forest service lookout at Mt. Ingalls in August 1930
Register gives 1936 for the tower; the Quincy marker says Company 989 of the CCC built it in 1935
Clark Hart took the post in June 1936
Mrs. Harry Kelley stationed at the Forest Service lookout (September 1943 item)
Lois Olds, an artist, had spent three years as a lookout and was back for 1946
Chosen as one of three Northern California lookouts for a time-lapse camera study with the State Forestry Division and the Weather Bureau
September 1962: a bullet fragmented on the catwalk and struck lookout Jim Bailey in six places; he stayed at his post until a replacement came
September 1976: station closed down and not to reopen the next year except in emergencies
Structure dismantled and moved to the Plumas County Fairgrounds in Quincy; the marker says a Navy Reserve construction battalion dismantled and rebuilt it there
The lookout was moved to the Quincy Fairgrounds.
